raw_question_text: Draw the curve traced out by an end of a thin wire unwound from a regular hexagone of side 15 mm, the wire being kept tight . Draw a tangent and normal to the curve at a point 80 mm from the center of the hexagon.

An area of 50 sq.km of a field is represented by an area of 150 sq.cm on a map. Construct a diagonal scale to read kilometers, hectometers and decameters. The maximum length to be indicated on the scale is 10 km. Show a distance of 6.48 km on the scale.

The end A of a line AB is in the HP and 15 mm in front of the VP. The end B is 50 mm behind the VP and 40 mm below the HP. The distance between the end projectors is 50 mm. Draw the projections of AB and determine its true length and true inclinations with the two planes.
Draw the projections of a regular pentagon of 40 mm side having its surface inclined at 300 to V.P and side on which it rest on V.P makes an angle of 600 with H.P.

Draw the projections of a cone with base 45 mm diameter and axis 60 mm long when it is resting on the ground on a point of its base circle with the axis making an angle of 30 0 with HP and 450 with VP.

A square prism of 32 mm side and 100 mm height is lying on its base on HP such that the edges of the base are equally inclined to VP. The prism is cut by a section plane passing through the mid-point of the axis such that the true shape of section is a rhombus of diagonals of 102 mm and 42 mm. Determine the inclination of section plane with HP.

A cone having diameter of base 75 mm axis 75 long is resting on its base on HP. It is cut by a section plane perpendicular to VP and inclined at 40 0 to HP and cutting the axis at a point 40 mm from base. Draw the development of the part of the cone containing the apex.

A cylinder of 75 mm diameter standing on its base on HP is completely penetrated by another cylinder of 55 mm diameter with their axes intersecting at right angle. Draw the projections showing the lines of intersection, assuming that the axis of the smaller cylinder is parallel to VP. 23-08-18AM
By using the following views as shown in figure 1, draw the isometric view. All dimensions are in mm. Use a scale of 1:20.
For the following isometric view shown in figure 2 , draw a) Front view by seeing from 60 mm width side b) top view c) left side view. All dimensions are in mm. Figure: 2 23-08-18AM
A point F is 50 mm from a line AB. a point P is moving in a plane such that the ratio of its distances from F and line AB remains constant and equals to 2/3, draw locus of point P.
Draw involute of a pentagon of side 25 mm.
Construct a scale of 1:40 to read metres, decimetres and centimetres and long enough to measure up to 6 m. Mark a distance of 4.76 m on it.

A line AB, 80 mm long, makes an angle of 3 0° with the VP, and lies in a plane perpendicular to both the HP and VP. Its end A is in the HP, and the end B is in the VP. Draw its projections and show its traces.
A semi-circular lamina of 64mm diameter has its straight edge in VP and i nclined at an angle of 45° to HP. The surface of the lamina makes an angle of 30° with VP. Draw the projections.
Draw the projection of a pentagonal prism, base 20 mm side and axis 50mm long, resting on one of its rectangular faces on the ground with the axis inclined at 30° to the VP.

A cylinder, 60 mm diameter and 80 mm long, has its axis parallel to the H.P. and inclined at 30° to V.P. It is cut by a vertical section plane in such a way that the true shape of the section is an ellipse having the major axis 7 0 mm long. Draw its sectional front view and true shape of the section.

A cylinder of diameter 50 mm and height 75 mm is resting on the ground on its flat end. It is cut by a sectional plane inclined at 30 0 to the axis of the cylinder and passing through a point on the axis at height of 50 mm from the base. Draw the lateral surface of the bottom part.

A cone of base diameter 80 mm and its axis 100 mm is resting on its base on HP. It is completely penetrated by a cylinder of base diameter of 40 mm. The axes of the solids intersect each other at right angles, 30 mm above the base of the cone. Draw the projections of the combination and curves of intersection.
Draw isometric view of a cylinder of base diameter 55 mm and axis length 65 mm when the axis of the cylinder is (a) vertical (b) horizontal.
Draw (a) Front View (b) Top View (c) Side view for the below figure. (All dimensions are in mm).
The actual length of 300 m is represented by a line of 10 cm on a drawing. Draw a vernier scale to read up to 500 m. Mark on it a length of 367 m.
Draw a regular heptagon having 40 mm long sides, using general method.

Draw the locus of a point P moving so that the ratio of the distance from a fixed point F to its distance from a fixed straight line is 0.75. Point P is at a distance of 70 mm from the straight line. Also, draw the tangent and normal to the curve.

A circular plate of 60 mm diameter has a hexagonal hole of 20 mm side, centrally punched. Draw the projections of the plate, resting on HP on a point, with its surface inclined at 30 0 to HP. Any two parallel sides o f the hexagonal hole are perpendicular to VP. Draw the projections of the plate.
A 90 mm long line PQ is inclined at 300 to the HP and 450 to the VP. The end P is 15 mm above the HP and 25 mm in front of VP. Draw its projections , locate the traces in the following two cases.
When the end Q is in the first quadrant
When the end Q is in the third quadrant.

A cone of base diameter 50 mm and axis length 75 mm, resting on HP on its base is cut by a plane i nclined at 45 0 to HP and perpendicular to VP and is bisecting the axis. Draw the front view and development of lateral surface of bottom part.
Draw the front view, top view and side view of the object shown in the figure. All dimensions are in mm.

An area of 200 cm2 on a map represents 50 km 2 of actual land area. Draw a diagonal scale to measure a distance up to a single decametre. Mark off the following distances on the scale: (i) 5 km, 7 hectometres and 6 decametres, (ii) 3.04 km and (iii) 458 decametres.

A semicircle of 50 mm diameter has a straight line AB of 80 mm length tangent to it at the end point, A of its diameter AC. Draw the paths of the end points A and B of the straight line AB, when AB rolls on the semicircle without slipping. Name the Curve.

A straight line AB has its end A 15 mm above the HP and 10 mm in front of the VP. The other end B is 25 mm in front of the VP. The VT is 10 mm above the HP. Draw the projections of the line if the distance between end projectors is 25 mm and find its true length and true angles of inclination with the HP and the VP. Locate the HT.
Draw the projections of a triangular plate of 30 mm sides, with one of its sides AB in the VP and with its surface inclined at 600 to the VP.

A cylinder of diameter 50 mm and length of the axis 65 mm has its axis parallel to the VP and inclined at 300 to the HP. It is cut by a cutting plane perpendicular to the HP, inclined at 300 to the VP, and passing through a point P on the axis 25 mm from the top end. Draw the top view, the sectional front view, and the true shape of the section of the cylinder.

A cone of base diameter 80 mm and axis 100 mm, is resting on its base on the H.P. It is completely penet rated by a cylinder of base diameter 40 mm. The axes of the solids intersect each other at right angles, 30 mm above the base of the cone. Draw the projections of the combination and show curves of intersection.

A cylinder of diameter 50 mm and length of the axis 65 mm rests on its base with the axis perpendicular to the HP. It is cut by the cutting plane perpendicular to the VP, inclined at 450 to the HP and passing through a point on axis 25 mm from the top. Draw the front view, the sectional top view, and the development of the lateral surface of the cylinder. (Contd…)
Pictorial view of an object is shown in figure. Using first angle projection, draw its (a) full sectional front view, (b) top view and (c) side view. (All dimensions are in mm).

Construct a vernier scale to read the distances corrected to decameter on a map in which the actual distances are reduced in the ratio of 1:50,000. The scale should be long enough to measure 8 km. Mark a length of 4.82 km o n scale by constructing backward vernier scales.

A circus man rides a motor -cycle inside a globe of 4 m diameter. The motorcycle wheel diameter is 0.8 m. Draw the locus of a point spot on the circumference of the motor -cycle wheel for its one complete turn. Adopt a suitable scale.
The ordinate of a point P on the curve is 40 mm and is at a distance of 20 mm from the vertex. Draw the parabola.
Draw a diagonal scale of RF = 1/20,000 to show kilometres and decimals of kilometre. Mark on the scale the distances 1.64 km and 2.37 km.

The projections of a line AB are perpendicular to xy. The end A is in the HP and 50 mm in front of the VP and the end B is in the VP and 40 mm above the HP. Draw its projections, determine its true length and the inclinations with the reference planes.

The top view ‘ abc’ of a triangle ABC is an equilateral triangle of side 50 mm, ab being inclined at 45 0 to xy. The point A is in the V.P. and 35 mm abov e the ground, while the points B and C are on the ground. Draw the projections of the triangle and determine its true shape.

A cylinder of base diameter 50 mm and axis 70 mm is lying on a generator on the HP with its axis parallel to the VP. It is cut by an A.P. inclined at 30 0 to the HP and passing through a point on the axis 30 mm from one of its ends. Draw its sectional top view and obtain true shape of the section.

A pentagonal pyramid, side of base 35 mm and axis 70 mm long, is lying on one of its corners on the HP such that the triangular surface opposite to the corner is parallel to HP and perpendicular to VP, and the base edge containing that triangular surface is parallel to both the HP and VP. Draw the projections of the solid when the apex of the pyramid is nearer to the observer.

A cone of 100 mm diameter and axis 120 mm long, resting on its base in the HP is penetrated by a horizontal cylinder 50 mm diameter and 120 mm long. The axis of t he cylinder is 30 mm above the base of the cone and parallel to the VP. If the axis of the cylinder is 5 mm in front of the axis of the cone, draw the projections of the solids showing the curves of intersection.

A cuboid of sides 40 mm × 60 mm × 40 mm is resting on its longer side in the H.P. and one its longer surfaces parallel to the V.P. It is cut by a section plane perpendicular to V.P. and incline to the H.P. such that it passes diagonally from one corner of the top to the opposite corner of the bottom. Develop the lateral surface o f the bottom part of cuboid.
Draw top, front and side views of the isometric projection given in Figure.1. All dimensions are in mm.
Draw the isom etric view of the object whose orthographic projections are given in Figure.2. All dimensions are in mm.
Construct an Ellipse when the distance of focus from the directrix is equal to 60 mm and eccentricity is 2/3. Draw Tangent and Normal to the curve at a distance of 80 mm from directrix.
Divide a Straight line of 70 mm into 11(eleven) equal parts.
Construct a diagonal scale of RF= 1/(6250) to read upto 1 Kilometer and to read meters on it. Show a distance of 653 meters on it.
Show by means of a drawing that when the diameter of the directing c ircle is twice that of the generating circle, the Hypocycloid is a straight line. Take the diameter of generating circle is 50 mm.
A Rectangle plane of EFGH of size 60 mm × 30 mm has a corner E on H.P. and 20 mm in-front of V.P. The longer side of rectangle is inclined at 70 0 to H.P. and parallel to V.P. Draw its projections.

A line CD of 60mm length is inclined at an angle of 30 0 to H.P. and 450 to V.P. The Point C is 20 mm above H.P. and 15 mm in-front of V.P. and 80 mm from Right profile plane. Draw i) Front View ii) Top view iii) Left side view of the line.

A line AB, of 90 mm long, is inclined at 45 0 to HP and its top view makes an angle of 60 0 with XY. The end A is on HP and 12 mm in -front of VP. Draw its projections, Traces and find its inclination with VP.

Two points A and B are on HP, the point A bei ng 30 mm in -front of VP while B is 45 mm behind VP. The line joining their top views makes an angle of 450 with XY. Find horizontal distance between the two points.
A Pentagonal pyramid of base 20 mm and axis 50 mm has its triangular face in the VP with a shorter side inclined to the HP at 300. Draw its projections

A Pentagonal prism of edge of base 30 mm and axis 60 mm long is resting on one of its faces on HP. The axis of t he prism is parallel to both HP and VP. It is cut by a section plane, inclined at 45 0 to HP and passing through the axis 15 mm from one of its base. Draw the projections and show the true shape of the section.

Draw the development of a Cy linder of 40 mm diameter and 60 mm height, containing a square hole of 20 mm side. The sides of the hole are equally incl ined to the base and the axis of the hole bisects the axis of the cylinder.

A vertical cylinder of 70 mm diameter is penetrated by a horizontal cylinder of the same size. The axis of the penetrating cylinder is 12 mm away from the axis of the vertical cylinder. Draw the projections of the cylinders and showing the lines (curves) of intersection.
Draw the Front view, Top view and side view of the object shown in figure. All dimensions are in mm.

Draw the Perspective view of a vertical circular plane of 50 mm diameter, in clined at 300 to the Picture plane (P.P). The center of the plane is 25 mm behind the P.P. It is resting on a point on the circumference on the ground. The station point is located in the central plane passing through the cent er of t he circular plane and 80 mm in -front of P.P. and 70 mm above the ground.
Draw the Isometric projection of a circular lamina of 60 mm diameter, when its surface is Vertical.

MN is vertical line of length 90 mm and represents the minor axis of an ellipse. A point P is located 90 mm from M and 50 mm from N, so that it lies on that ellipse. Draw the ellipse and find its major axis length and eccentricity.

A train is running at a speed of 40 km/hr. Construct a plane scale to read up to a km and a minute. The scale should measure up to 50 km. The RF of the scale is 1:25000. On the scale show the distance covered by the train in 39 minutes.

The front view of a line AB 80 mm long measures 55 mm while its top view measures 70 mm. End A is in both HP and VP. Draw the projections of the line and find its inclination with the reference planes.

A regular hexagonal lamina with its edge 50 mm has its plane inclined at 45 0 to H.P and lying with one of its edges in H.P. The plane of one of its diagonals is inclined at 45 0 to XY. The corner nearest to VP is 15mm infront of it. Draw its projections.

The hexagonal pyramid base 30 mm side and axis 60 mm long has one of its slant edges on HP such that two of its triangular faces containing the slant edge on which it rests are equally inclined to HP. The top view of the axis appears to be inclined at 450 to VP. Draw its projections when its base is nearer to the observer than its apex.

A pentagonal pyramid of 25mm base side and 60mm height is resting on the HP on a corner of its base in such way a that the base makes 500 to HP. One of the base edges is perpendicular to VP. It is cut by a section plane perpendicular to HP and inclined to VP at 30 0 such that the section plane is 6mm in front of the top end of the axis of the pyramid. Draw the sectional top vie w, sectional front view and the true shape of the section.

A cylinder 50 mm in diameter and the axi s 65 mm long is resting on its base with its axis perpendicular to the H.P . It is cut by a cutting plane perpendicular to V.P inclined at 45 0 to the HP and passing through a point on the axis 25mm from the top. Draw the front view, sectional top view and development of lateral surface of the bottom part of the cylinder.

A cylinder of 65 mm diameter standing on its base on HP is completely penetrated by another cylinder of 45 mm diameter with their axes intersecting at right angle. Draw the projections showing the lines of intersection, assuming that the axis of the smaller cylinder is parallel to VP.

A right regular hexagonal prism of side of base 25 mm and altitude 55 mm has a square hole of 20 mm side at the center. The axes of the prism and the hole coincide. One of the faces of the square hole is parallel to one of the faces of the hexagon. Draw the isometric projection with the hole.
For the isometric view shown below figure, draw a) front view b) top view and c) left side view. All dimensions are in mm.

The distance between Bombay and Poona is 180 Km. a passenger train covers this distance in 6 hours. Construct a plain scale to time upto a single minute. The R.F. of the scale is 1/200000. Find the distance covered by the train in 36 minutes.

A circle of 50 mm diameter rolls on a horizontal line for a half revolution and then on a vertical line for another half revolution. Draw the curve traced out by a point P on the circumference of the circle.

A line AB, 65 mm long has its end A 20 mm above the H.P. and 25 mm in front of the V.P. The end B is 40 mm above the H.P. and 65 mm in front of the V.P. Draw the projections of AB and show its inclinations with the H.P. and the V.P.
Draw the projections of a regular pentagon of 40 mm side, having its surface inclined at 300 to the H.P. and a side parallel to the H.P. and inclined at an angle of 60 0 to the V.P.

A square pyramid, base 50 mm side and axis 75 mm long, is resting on the H.P. on one of its triangular faces, the top view of the axis making an angle of 30 0 with the V.P. It is cut by a horizontal section plane, the V.T of which intersects the axis at a point 6 mm from the base. Draw the front view, sectional top view and the development of the sectioned pyramid.
Draw the isometric view of following casting as shown in figure . All dimensions are in mm.

A circle of 50 mm diameter rolls along a straight line without slipping. Draw the curve traced out by a point P on the circumference, for one complete revolution of the circle. Name the curve. Draw a tangent to the curve at a point on it 40 mm from the line.

A rectangular plot of land of area 16 sq. m is represented on a map by a similar rectangle of 1 square centimeter. Calculate the RF of the scale of the map. Construct a plain scale to measure up to 60 m and mark a distance of 46 m on the scale.
Draw the curve traced by a point on the circumference of a rolling circle, on a straight line for one and half revolution.

On the plan of a shopping complex, a line 10cm long represents a distance of 5m. Draw a diagonal scale for the plan to read up to 6m showing meters, decimetres and centimetres. Mark the lengths 3.24m and 5.57m.

A point A is situated in the first quadrant. Its shortest distance from the i ntersection point of HP and VP and auxiliary plane is 60 mm and it is equidistant from the principal planes. Draw the projections of the point and determine its distance from the principal planes.
The top view of a 75mm long line measures 55 mm. The line is in the VP, its one end being 25 mm above the HP. Draw its projections.

The top view of a plane is a regular pentagon of side 30 mm having one side inclined at 30° to the VP. Its front view is a straight line inclined at 45° to the reference line. Draw the projections of the plane and determine its true shape.

A pentagonal prism is resting on one of the corners of its base in the HP. The longer edge containing that corner is inclined at 30 ° to HP and the vertical plane containing that edge is inclined at 45° to the VP. Draw the projections of the solid.

A hexagonal pyramid of side of base 40 mm and height of axis 110 mm is resting on one of its inclined vertical faces on H.P. such that its axis remains parallel to the V.P. It is cut by a cutting plane which is inclined at an angle 45° with H.P. and bisecting the axis of the pyramid. Draw front view, sectional top view.

A pentagonal pyramid of base 30 mm side and height 70 mm, stands with its base on H.P such that one of the base edges is parallel to V.P. It is cut by a section plane perpendicular to V.P, inclined at 30° to H.P and bisecting its axis. Draw the development of the surface of the pyramid.

A cylinder of base diameter 70 mm is resting on its base on the HP. It is penetrated by another cylinder of base diameter 60 mm, such that their axes intersect each other at right angles. Draw the projections of the combination and show the curves of intersections.

A vertical cylinder of base diameter 50 mm and height 70 mm is cut by a plane inclined at 55° to HP and perpendicular to VP, which meets the axis at a distance of 20 mm from top base. Draw the isometric view of the remaining portion of the cylinder.
A sphere of 50 mm diameter is surrounded centrally on the top of a square bl ock of side 60 mm and thickness 20 mm. Draw the isometric view of the arrangement.
Draw the front view, side view and top view for the given figure. All dimensions are in mm

A circle of 50 mm diameter rolls inside another fixed circle of radius 80 mm. Draw the hypocycloid for the point P on the rolling circle, which is at the contact point of the fixed and rolling circles.
Construct a diagonal scale of RF = (1/4000) to show meters and long enough to measure 500 meters. Indicate on this a length of 374 meters.
Draw the projections of a circle of 50 mm diameter w hen its plane is equally inclined to the HP and VP. One end of a diameter of the circle touches the HP while the other end touches the VP.

A pentagonal prism of 30 mm base side and height 50 mm is standing on the HP on its base, with one side of base perpendicular to VP. This prism is cut by a section plane 40 0 inclined to HP through mid -point of the axis. Draw the front view, sectional top view, and sectional side view. Draw also the true shape of the section.

A cube of side 30 mm rests on its base in the HP with a vertical face inclined at 30 0 to the VP. It is cut by a plane perpendicular to the VP and inclined at 50 0 to the HP, and the top portion of cube is removed. The plane bisects the axis of the cube. Draw the development of the frustum of the cube.

A rectangular prism 40 × 30 × 15 mm rests on the ground on one of its ends with one of the longest edges touching the PP and one of the shortest edges receding to the left at angle of 40 0 to the PP. The nearest vertical edge is 15 mm to the left of the station point which is at a distance of 55 mm in front of the PP and 30 mm above the ground. Draw the perspective view of the prism.
Three views of a so lid are shown in the figure below. Draw the isometric projection of the solid. All dimensions are in mm.
